book_title: Chapter 9: The Decision — Bull vs. Bear, Scenarios & Exit Playbook
question: How do we balance Arista's elite compounder franchise against the $172.09 stop breach, Stage 4 breakdown, and ex-SBC valuation compression?

epigraph.quote: The best way to measure your investing success is not by whether you're beating the market but by whether you've put in place a financial plan and a behavioral discipline that are likely to get you where you want to go.
epigraph.author: Benjamin Graham

web_blocks.title: 9.1 Steelmanning Both Sides: The Bull Case vs. The Bear Case

web_blocks.html: The Bull Case ($215): Arista remains an asset-light networking leader. It holds $14.36 billion in cash with zero debt [2][22]. Return on invested capital stands at 28.89%, and 9M 2026 GAAP operating margin reached 44.4% [2][22]. Q3 sales rose 58.5% YoY to $3.66 billion, while total RPO reached $8.6 billion (91% recognizable within two years) [2][3]. On November 17, Arista launched 5nm R4 switches for distributed AI inferencing with up to 60% lower power use [28]. If Arista hits ~$18.5 billion in FY2027 sales with >=63% gross margins and sustains a 19.6% 10-year revenue CAGR, ex-SBC diluted DCF supports a $215.00 Bull value (~29.3x FY28E EPS) [3][24].

The Bear Case ($115 / $109 Stressed): Concentration, dilution, and NVIDIA rivalry hit together. Microsoft (26%) and Meta (16%) drive 42% of sales, while two resellers hold 52% of receivables [1]. On November 17, NVIDIA revealed Meta is expanding Spectrum-X and BlueField-4 networking, extended NVLink Fusion to custom XPUs, and partnered with Cisco on USFP optics [30]. Meanwhile, 9M GAAP gross margin fell 160 bps YoY to 62.9%, and FCF conversion eased to 104.8% [2]. Evaluation inventory doubled to $874.3 million, and purchase commitments hit $11.4 billion without Broadcom or EMS exclusivity [1][2]. Buybacks stayed at $0 alongside $1.7 billion of unamortized RSUs and steady insider sales [2][31][33]. Under a 12.0% CAGR and 10.0% WACC, ex-SBC value falls to $115.00 ($109.31 with -200 bps margin stress).

Deducting 4.0% SBC (37.0% FCF margin) across 1.2782 billion diluted shares resets our 12-month grid from $125 / $200 / $240 down to $115 / $180 / $215. Expected value falls to $167.50 (-0.1% vs. CMP), confirming zero valuation margin of safety.

web_blocks.html: Red Team Stress Test & Hinge Claim: Shifting weights to 10% Bull ($215), 40% Base ($180), and 50% Bear at the $110.00 stressed floor ($109.31 at 35.0% FCF margin, 10.0% WACC) cuts expected value to $148.50 (-11.4% vs. CMP). Waiting to reclaim the $177.78 30-week SMA yields just +$2.22 upside to $180.00 (+1.2%) against -$43.95 risk to $133.83 Pivot S2 (0.05:1 R:R, or 0.18:1 against a 1.0x ATR stop). Even at the $149.07–$153.61 Pivot S1 shelf, a genuine 1.56x ATR14 stop at $133.83 yields 1.33:1 R:R (<1.50:1). Our hinge claim: Arista must convert $8.6 billion RPO into ~$18.0B–$18.5B of FY2027 sales at >=62% GAAP gross margin and burn down $874.3M evaluation inventory cleanly [2][28][30]. That breaks if February 2027 Q4 results guide FY2027 sales below $17.0B, gross margin breaks below 61%, or Note 3 shows evaluation-gear write-downs [2].

That totals an unrealized loss of -$862.35 (-11.50%) on a $7,499.96 cost basis. On November 20, the $167.62 facts close ($167.66 TV) broke our locked $172.09 stop on 1.67x volume and sliced below the 50-day, 30-week, and 200-day averages. Our stop rule requires selling all 39.599149 shares immediately (holding_shares_to_sell: 39.599149). Exiting trims a 2.43-beta stock inside a 9-stock AI cluster (40.31% of your $75,110.60 net worth) and raises $6,637.61 in cash.

First (TREND), ANET sits in STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED, AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN) with intraday_4h_turn: false inside a 10-distribution-day market Downtrend. book_paragraphs: We reach the moment where research turns into action, and discipline earns its keep. On the business side, Arista Networks remains an extraordinary engineering franchise: $14.36 billion in cash with zero debt, 44.4% nine-month operating margins, 28.89% return on invested capital, and $8.6 billion in remaining performance obligations backed by new 5-nanometer R4 distributed inferencing switches.

Yet three hard truths force an unambiguous exit on held shares and a Rejected verdict on new capital. First, nine-month gross margin compressed 160 basis points to 62.9% while evaluation inventory doubled to $874.3 million. Second, deducting 4.0% stock-based compensation and using 1.2782 billion diluted shares cuts our Base fair value to $180.00—leaving virtually zero upside above the $177.78 30-week average. Third, Friday's 11.57% plunge on 1.67 times volume shattered our locked $172.09 structural stop and pushed every timeframe into a Stage 4 breakdown.

book_subsections.title: Why You Must Execute the $172.09 Stop Without Hesitation
paragraphs: In our November 13 monograph, we wrote down the rule in plain ink: exit the entire position immediately on any close below $172.09. We did not pick that number arbitrarily; it sat half an ATR below the 30-week moving average to separate normal volatility from genuine trend failure. On November 20, Arista closed at $167.62 in facts ($167.66 on TradingView), slicing beneath the 50-day, 30-week, and 200-day averages in one stroke.

Never widen a stop on a losing position to comfort your fundamental conviction. Across Schwab (29.4043 shares) and Robinhood (10.194849 shares), you own 39.599149 shares worth $6,637.61—an 8.84% weight in a 2.43-beta stock that sits inside a nine-name tech and semiconductor cluster moving in lockstep across 40.31% of your net worth. Your action for existing shares is EXIT IMMEDIATELY: sell all 39.599149 shares, lock the -$862.35 loss while it is still small, and raise $6,637.61 in dry powder.

book_subsections.title: Why New Capital Is Rejected Rather Than Hedged Into Wait for Support
paragraphs: Deducting 4.0% stock-based compensation and dividing by 1.2782 billion diluted shares lowers our 12-month scenario grid to Bull $215.00 (20%), Base $180.00 (50%), and Bear $115.00 (30%), blending to a $167.50 expected value (-0.1% vs. CMP). Under a Red Team stress test (10% Bull, 40% Base, 50% Bear at the $110.00 stressed floor), expected value falls to $148.50 (-11.4%). At $167.66, you are paying fair value for a stock falling in Stage 4.

Even more decisively, no entry path clears our 1.50-to-1 reward-to-risk minimum. Entering after Arista reclaims its $177.78 30-week average offers only $2.22 of upside to $180.00 against $43.95 of downside to Pivot S2 ($133.83)—a 0.05-to-1 ratio. Even waiting for Pivot S1 ($149.07–$153.61) with a realistic 1.56x ATR stop at Pivot S2 ($133.83) yields only 1.33-to-1. Refusing to hedge a failed risk-reward setup with Wait for Support keeps our decision rule honest: new capital is Rejected on Valuation and Trend.

book_subsections.title: Why Cash Wins 100% of the Exit Proceeds
paragraphs: Where should the $6,637.61 proceeds go? Retain 100% in USD cash. Your Schwab account currently holds just $22.43 in cash, total portfolio cash sits at $2,540.35 (3.38% of net worth), and our Downtrend rule calls for a 22% cash buffer while effective portfolio beta exposure sits at 234.2%.

Adding $6,637.61 lifts consolidated cash to $9,177.96 (12.22% of net worth). Even though Shortlist leader AbbVie ($286.20, Stage 2, 1.85:1 support ratio) looks far healthier than ANET, we hold 0% there today until market breadth heals, and we assign 0% to Outside Stage 2 comparator Teradata ($35.45) because 1.39% revenue growth and 7.53% operating margins offer only 0.21-to-1 support-zone reward-to-risk.

book_subsections.title: What Would Re-Open Arista for Fresh Underwriting
paragraphs: Exiting a great business on a stop loss and rejecting fresh capital on valuation is risk control, not permanent prejudice. Four concrete proof points would earn Arista a fresh review: first, a multi-week Stage 1 base and high-volume reclaim of the 30-week average ($177.78); second, either a deeper price reset or upward cash-flow revisions that restore at least 1.50-to-1 reward-to-risk on a full 1.0x-ATR stop.

Third, February 2027 Q4 earnings must confirm FY2027 revenue of $18.0 billion to $18.5 billion with GAAP gross margins at or above 62%. Fourth, footnote 3 must show verifiable burn-off of the $874.3 million customer evaluation inventory and $11.4 billion purchase commitments without write-downs. Until all four gates clear, your capital works harder—and sleeps far better—in cash.

book_subsections.title: Tracking the Three Horizon Checkpoints Over the Next Year
paragraphs: Keep your monitoring checklist simple across three horizons. Over the next one to three months, stay completely out of ANET while it trades below its 30-week average ($177.78) in a Downtrend market, watching whether Pivot S1 ($149.07–$153.61) or Pivot S2 ($133.83) arrests the slide. Over six to eighteen months, judge February 2027 Q4 results strictly against ~$18.0B–$18.5B FY2027 revenue, >=62% gross margin, and shrinking evaluation inventory.

Over three to five years, Arista's $14.36 billion net cash, EOS software stickiness, and 5nm R4 inferencing platform keep it an elite business worth tracking. Respecting a stop loss today preserves the capital you will need when valuation and trend align again.
